text:
maria: customer hitting 401 invalid_api_key after rotating their key. they copied the key from their password manager and pasted into curl, still 401. any quick ideas?

 tom: can you paste the curl (redact the key) and tell me OS/browser and clipboard tool?

 maria: curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings" -d '{"input":"test"}'
 using Chrome on Windows 10, they use ClipboardFusion to manage clips.

 tom: ask them to run this on the machine to show hidden bytes: 
 ```
 echo -n '<PASTED_KEY>' | xxd -p | sed -n '1p'
 ```
 paste the output.

 maria: they ran it, returned:
 ```
 7b5c727466313030...
 ```
 that prefix (7b5c727466) decodes to "{\\rtf" — looks like RTF data at the start of the copied string.

 sarah: yup, ClipboardFusion (and a few password managers) can put rich-text/RTF variants on the clipboard. if the app or paste method picks the wrong clipboard flavour you end up with the RTF wrapper bytes included in the token. that will break the HMAC/lookup and return 401.

 tom: repro steps i tried locally: store a key in an RTF field, copy via clipboard tool, paste into a terminal input — the paste can include the literal RTF header. quick diagnostic: 
 ```
 printf '%s' '<PASTED_KEY>' | xxd -p | head -c 20
 # if you see 7b5c727466 ("{\\rtf") it's RTF-wrapped
 ```

 maria: customer confirmed: they accidentally pasted the RTF clipboard entry from Windows clipboard history instead of the plain-text clip. when they used "paste as plain text" into Notepad and re-copied the visible token, the API call worked.

 support-bot: ticket #12345 updated: root cause = RTF wrapper bytes in API key copy. remediation actions: rotated key for customer, advise copy-as-plain-text, add note to support KB.

 tom: followups / preventative: 1) ask customers to use the dashboard copy button (copies plain text) or a plain-text editor as intermediary; 2) docs: add short section about clipboard managers and RTF/HTML flavours; 3) server-side: validate token charset/format early and return a clearer error (e.g., 401 + "invalid_api_key: unexpected characters") instead of generic 401.

 maria: rotated the key and confirmed success with customer, they were happy on the call. closing on our side :white_check_mark:

 sarah: adding KB stub: "If you see 401 after copying a key, paste into a plain-text editor and verify there are no RTF/HTML headers or invisible bytes (run xxd -p)."

 tom: thanks — tagging devex and docs to add note.
